title: Resilient span relay with prioritized retry and backend transform hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Replace the current simple OTLP passthrough with a resilient span relay that provides prioritized retries, per-backend transformation hooks, and bounded buffering with spillover to disk. This relay sits between our ingest tier and exporter layer and must support per-tenant prioritization, sampling-aware retry policies, and backend-specific field mapping for Tempo and Jaeger.

Motivation: We see spikes of dropped spans under transient exporter errors and uneven downstream behavior between Tempo and Jaeger. Customers (especially enterprise tenants) lose high-value spans during short outages. A specialized relay will reduce loss, let us adapt export format mappings without touching SDKs, and centralize retry/backpressure behavior.

Scope: Build relay service with: 1) in-memory ordered buffer with priority lanes (high: paid-tenants & sampled spans, normal: regular spans), 2) prioritized exponential backoff retry queue with per-backend and per-tenant rate limits, 3) durable spillover to local disk when memory threshold crossed, 4) plugin-style transform hooks for per-backend mapping (tempo/jaeger tag normalization, trace ID formats), 5) metrics and dashboards for buffer occupancy, retry successes/failures, tail latency introduced by relay, and 6) integration test harness that simulates exporter failures and validates no-loss semantics for high-priority spans.

Non-goals: Long-term storage of traces, full tail-based sampling engine (we will ingest sampling decisions included in OTLP attributes), rewriting ingest SDKs, or implementing full tenant billing within relay.

Proposed design notes: - Relay accepts OTLP/gRPC streams and forwards to configured exporter adapters. - Write-ahead file on disk will be an append-only segment store with configurable retention and compaction. - Priority lanes are implemented as separate queues; the dispatcher polls high-priority queue preferentially but enforces fairness to avoid starvation. - Transform hooks are small WASM modules (or Go plugins initially) that perform attribute normalization, tag renaming, and trace-id canonicalization. - Backpressure signal: relay exposes status endpoint and emits metrics; smart-router can observe these metrics and route traffic to fallback models/endpoints.

Trade-offs considered: - Using WASM for hooks increases isolation but adds runtime complexity; initial implementation will use in-process Go hook interface, migrate to WASM if we observe security or isolation needs. - Durable disk spillover complexity vs acceptable data loss: we choose spillover to reduce customer-visible loss for short outages, but enforce TTL to avoid unbounded disk growth.

Acceptance criteria and tests are enumerated below.
acceptance_criteria: Relay accepts OTLP/gRPC and forwards to Tempo and Jaeger exporter adapters successfully in normal operation
High-priority spans (tenant-tagged) are retained and retried during exporter outages until success or until configured TTL expires
In-memory buffer spills to disk under high memory pressure and recovers correctly on restart
Transform hooks can remap a common "http.status_code" attribute to "status_code" for Jaeger and add "service_name" fallback for Tempo
End-to-end tests simulate exporter flaps and prove <1% loss for high-priority spans and specified SLOs for normal spans
New metrics emitted: relay_buffer_size, relay_disk_segments, relay_retry_rate, relay_priority_latency_p95, relay_export_failures_total
Documentation and runbook created; basic alerting rules and dashboards deployed to staging Grafana
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after discussion with PM and infra. Initial design agreed in sync; assigned to Marco.

2025-02-14 Marco Nguyen: Spike complete — validated basic prioritized in-memory queues and local file append segments. Memory threshold and spillover logic tested under a synthetic load. Patch in repo: PR#238.
2025-02-18 Priya Singh (SRE): Reviewed approach; requested backpressure signal and health API that the smart-router can consume. Added requirement for per-tenant export rate limits.
2025-02-22 Elena Ruiz (PM): Marked customer impact as medium. Requested inclusion of enterprise tenant prioritization and brief runbook for incident on-call.
2025-02-25 Marco Nguyen: Implemented transform-hook interface and two adapters for Tempo/Jaeger field mapping. Basic unit tests added. See PR#243.
2025-02-28 QA: Began chaos tests simulating exporter 503s and disk IO slowdowns. Observed retry storm on restart; added jitter to retry backoff and drain pacing to prevent thundering herd.

2025-03-03 Marco Nguyen: Canary deployment to staging relay cluster started (3 replicas). Metrics look good; priority queue p95 latency ~12ms, normal queue p95 ~45ms under synthetic 2000rps. Follow-up: tune disk compaction and add idle segment GC.
rollout_plan: Build feature flags to enable relay per-cluster and per-tenant
Deploy to staging with synthetic load and exporter chaos experiments
Canary to 5% of hosted traffic with enterprise tenants routed to relay
Monitor metrics and error budgets for 48h, iterate on pacing and retry windows
Gradually increase to 100% after no regressions and runbook verified
